quote: ResourceManager.as:41 `internal static var resourceFileNameArray:Array = ["shs3resource.swf","musicresource.swf","soundresource.swf","imageresource.swf","bgresource.swf"];` :186 `ba = decryptByteArray(ba,resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1));` :205 `for(var i:int = 3; i < 256; i++)` :207 `if(i % 11 == 0)` :213 `ba[i] ^= key;`
text: The XOR key for the five obfuscated Android resource blobs is NOT one constant - it is the SECOND CHARACTER of the resource's filename, so every blob has its own key. ResourceManager.as:186 passes 'resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1)' into decryptByteArray, and :41 lists the five filenames. That yields shs3resource.swf -> 'h' = 104, musicresource.swf -> 'u' = 117, soundresource.swf -> 'o' = 111, imageresource.swf -> 'm' = 109, bgresource.swf -> 'g' = 103. This reconciles the two keys the Stage-0 brief already carries (C1's 109 from Mobile.as:352 and C3's 111 for the sound blob) and predicts the other three. Also note decryptByteArray only touches bytes 3..255 (swapping every i%11==0 byte with i+256), which is why the files still begin with a readable 'CWS' magic.

build: both — the point IS the difference
lane_impact: Cross-lane, and it hardens ⚠ S0-3 from a hedge into a proven hazard: web and android combat/progression tuning demonstrably diverge on four of six stat caps.
text: A hard, measured counterexample to build parity, found while checking the 271-cap claim. The stat-panel add-button gates are the same function in both builds but carry DIFFERENT formulas. ATK/DEF/SPD: android InventoryUI.as:2410-2412 gate on 'charlevel + 10' (90 at level 80); web §1t5957s0§.as:3344-3346 gate on '1 + (level + 10) * 3' (271 at level 80) — a 3x lift. MAXHP: android :2407 '10 + (charlevel + 10) * 5' (460); web :3341 '10 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 10' (910) — doubled. MAXAP: android :2409 '20 + (charlevel + 10)' (110); web :3343 '30 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 5' (480) — more than 4x. MAXCHI is the only one identical: android :2408 and web :3342 are both '10 + (lvl + 10) * 5' = 460. This is exactly the shape of divergence the S0-3 caveat warns about, now with numbers: the data XMLs match row for row, but progression tuning does NOT. Any INFERRED progression number ported from an android artifact must be re-derived web-side before it is called CONTRACT.

lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core: an argument-order bridge that names six web fields from android symbols without diffing a file against itself - reusable wherever a web/android pair shares a call signature.
text: C2 says the four data XMLs are android-side, so diffing them proves nothing, and that combat tuning parity is NOT established. Here is a bridge that is not circular. Android StatsManager.as:1834 calls `player.initPlayer(0, HP, MAXHP, CHI, MAXCHI, DEFENSE, getBaseReload(), getMinDamage(), getDamageRange(), getBaseSlashLength(), getSlashUsage(), getStat(1000), getStat(1001), getStat(1002), getLevel())` - fifteen named arguments. The web fighter's ctor §1t99s0§.as:188-201 takes exactly fifteen ints and assigns them in exactly that order, including `this.defense = param6` at the DEFENSE slot, which pins the alignment independently. That decodes six obfuscated web fields at once (§1t3257s0§=MAXHP, §1t4413s0§=MAXCHI, §1t4421s0§/§1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§ = skills 1000/1001/1002, §1t4420s0§=baseSlashLength) and it is what actually rules out an off-by-one in the mastery term.

lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: build the WEB behaviour (persistent on-bar empty-state label), not the android hover tooltip - and record this as a discharged C2 instance: the two builds' battle HUDs are NOT at parity on this element.
text: The packet notes that string 960 is unresolvable from the android table but not why, and the mechanism is a genuine, first-hand v0.717-vs-v0.682 divergence - one of the very few that discharges part of the C2 caveat instead of restating it. Android BattleUI.as:262 is the ENTIRE reload-bar text logic: `this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;` - the android build shows the crit text at full and nothing at all otherwise. It has no empty-state label on the bar. Instead its 'Change Stance' string lives on a mouse rollover over the portrait: :192-193 add MOUSE_OVER/MOUSE_OUT listeners on battlemodebust bound to showChangeStanceLabel/hideChangeStanceLabel (:430-440), which toggle changestancelabel and the bust highlight together. The web build replaced that hover affordance with a persistent on-bar notice, which is why getString(960) exists in v0.717 and is missing from the v0.682 table (strings.json["960"] returns None). Android also normalises the ratio itself before the call, while the web computes (reload-48)/(max-48) inside §1t5205s0§.

text: Correction to the lane_impact of the surviving BattleUI finding, which says the HUD needs 'a Change Stance button NEXT TO the portrait'. It is not next to the portrait — it IS the portrait. Android names the clickable §1t5158s0§ 'battlemodebust' (BattleUI.as:26), the same object that receives the player bust at :148 ('battlemodebust.bustcanvas.addChild(this.playerBust)') and carries the stance ring at :374 ('battlemodebust.stancecolor1.gotoAndStop(num)'). Android BattleUI.as:275-277 reads `if(this.battlemodebust.hitTestPoint(mousex,mousey)) { this.stanceButtonClick(); }`, and :112-113 set `battlemodebust.highlight.visible = false; battlemodebust.buttonMode = true;`. So §1t5158s0§ = battlemodebust. The stance COLOUR rides the same object: web §1t5208s0§ (:482-485) does `§1t5158s0§.§1t15895s0§.gotoAndStop(param1)` against android setStanceColor (:372-375) `battlemodebust.stancecolor1.gotoAndStop(num)`, called from the stance switch with 1=Light, 2=Balanced, 3=Heavy (§1t99s0§.as:3101, :3112, :3127). lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: ship the three-state meter label from the WEB contract; do not port android's two-line updateReload. Also: the 48 offset lives in the UI rescale, mirroring §1t99s0§.as:3050's gate.
text: String 960 and its grey label are not merely missing from the android string table — the android build has no code path that would use them. Android BattleUI.as:259-263 updateReload is two lines: 'this.reloadbar.bar.scaleX = percentage;' and 'this.crittext.visible = percentage >= 1 && this.reloadbar.visible;'. There is no ratio==0 branch and no second htmlText. The web v0.717 twin §1t113s0§.as:326-359 adds all three states (grey getString(960) at ratio 0, hidden at 0<r<1, black getString(175) + Snd_criticalDamage at r>=1) and rescales the input to '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' where android passes a pre-computed percentage. This explains why strings.json has no key '960' without needing a table-coverage argument, and it is a real, dated v0.682 -> v0.717 HUD change.

lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: ship ONE meter widget with three text states and a transition sound, not two separate crit/stance indicators. Also names the exact colours: #BBBBBB empty-state, #000000 full-state.
text: The packet stops at two of the third bar's three states. §1t113s0§.as:348-359 is the third: at ratio >= 1 the same TextField takes §1t5203s0§ = `"<font color='#000000'>" + getString(175) + "</font>"` (built at :110), i.e. BLACK 'Critical Hit', and :350-352 fire `§1t88s0§.instance.§1t1516s0§("Snd_criticalDamage")` on the transition into that state - guarded so it plays once, not per frame. So the single track under HP and Chi is a three-state readout on one 0..192 resource: empty -> #BBBBBB getString(960); filling -> no text; full -> #000000 getString(175) plus a one-shot sound. Under correction C3 the audio is recovered, so Snd_criticalDamage is a nameable, shippable stem rather than a TODO.

lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: before writing bar colours to config, find an artifact that binds colour to stat (a low-HP/death frame, or the SWF shape for hpbar). Do not inherit green=HP from prose on either side.
text: Nobody has established, from an artifact that ties COLOUR to STAT, that the green bar is HP and the blue bar is Chi. The code proves only that there are exactly two numeric updaters and one numeral-free one: android BattleUI.as:245-249 updateHp (hptext/hptextshadow/hpbar) and :252-256 updateChi (chitext/chitextshadow/chibar), whose web twins are §1t113s0§.as:312-317 (§1t5171s0§/§1t5172s0§/§1t5170s0§ = hptext/hptextshadow/hpbar) and :319-324 (§1t5165s0§/§1t5166s0§/§1t5164s0§ = chitext/chitextshadow/chibar), matched by call-order against the empty setReloadMax (:241-243) / §1t5200s0§ and updateReload/§1t5205s0§ that bracket them. Nothing in AS3 names a colour — the fills live in SWF art. The surviving 'video-study notes misread' finding asserts green=HP / blue=Chi, and B-11:7 asserts the exact opposite ('a thin green bar ... reads as a resource/stamina-type meter, NOT the blue HP bar ... a thick blue bar ... (this is HP)'). Circumstantial support for green=HP: REBUILD_READINESS.md:178 is Kheshav's own-eyes verdict on Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0 and reads 'player HP 20/20', and in that frame green is 20/20 while blue is 26/26; and across my three frames the green denominator is pinned at 20 (20/20, 14/20, 11/20) with its numerator falling during combat, while the blue denominator varies 26/31/47. That is inference plus one A5 line, not a colour-to-stat artifact. Flagging it because it would silently corrupt palette.ts and the config bar names, and because two committed docs currently disagree.
